name: Gazetteer Named Place Source Nodes
description: The PURE half of the GeoNames gazetteer lane (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only between modules, no JSON and no base64): it decodes a gazetteer dump into $GNP records and does nothing else. capabilities [], browser + wasmedge, request-scoped, no state between invocations; its one hostcall is the builtin plugin.getConfig (SDS $PIV, ConfigEntry list) for the operator's record cap geonames_limit. Every byte it decodes was fetched by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.http-request (an HttpResponse, HRSP) and every record it emits is persisted by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.storage-ingest; the scheduling and resume decisions live in the sibling com.digitalarsenal.data-source.geonames-ingest, exactly as cell-tower-source and cell-tower-ingest are split. THE JOB TRAVELS AS HttpRequest.CONTEXT: one size-prefixed $GNP header record per fetch (ID = the id prefix records are minted under, NAME = the text the job decodes, SOURCE = the dataset contract every record is published under), echoed in the HttpResponse and carried on into the text frame; it replaces the JSON job frame. The seed edition ships as a ZIP and there is no host unzip capability (and none may be added), so miniz 3.1.2 is vendored under vendor/miniz-3.1.2 (MIT, SHA-256 pinned and re-verified on every build) and the archive's central directory is walked in-guest. $GNP requires RESOLVED admin and country NAMES beside the codes, so the division/country files are inputs of parse_places and joined at parse time (the former parse_lookups method folded them into a JSON join table; no SDS record models one, so the join now happens in the one node that applies it). Run summaries, the inflate report and the tombstone list are FlowNotice (FNTC) frames.

sequentialJustification.detail: All three methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: inflate one archive member, decode tab-separated rows (joined against the lookup files) into records, decode tombstone rows into a list. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.displayName: Assemble and inflate the fetched edition

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (module-sdk runtime type HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, CONTEXT = the job ($GNP header).

inputPorts.description: The fetched edition as an HttpResponse, its job in CONTEXT. The job rides in the HttpResponse's CONTEXT: ONE size-prefixed $GNP header record geonames-ingest put in the request's CONTEXT and hostcap/http-request echoed - ID = the id prefix, NAME = the text the job decodes (the archive member of a .zip edition, empty = its first member), SOURCE = the dataset contract (DATASET_ID, DATASET_NAME, DATASET_URL, DATASET_EPOCH, SOURCE_URL, SOURCE_QUERY = the file selection, LICENSE, LICENSE_URL, ATTRIBUTION, SHARE_ALIKE, NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY).

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP): the fetched response verbatim (URL, STATUS, HEADERS, CONTEXT = the job, RETRIEVED_MS) with BODY replaced by the decoded gazetteer text.

outputPorts.description: The decoded gazetteer text, so no downstream node needs to know whether the edition arrived compressed. Not pushed on a 304.

acceptedTypeSets.description: FlowNotice (module-sdk runtime type FNTC): KIND Info REASON "inflated" COUNT = bytes out, or KIND Unchanged REASON "not-modified" on a 304; ITEMS container=, member=, bytes_in=, bytes_out=, status=; SOURCE_NAME = the dataset, AT_MS = its epoch.

outputPorts.description: Bytes in, bytes out, member name and upstream status for this assembly.

methods.description: Turns the fetched body into plain text. A job whose SOURCE_QUERY names a .zip walks the archive's CENTRAL DIRECTORY (never the local header, which carries zeroes under a data descriptor and would inflate to an empty gazetteer) and inflates the member the job's NAME names, or the first member when it names none; any other job (or a response with no job) passes the body through, which is what the daily modifications/deletes need. A 304 pushes no text and reports KIND Unchanged (the same-data ledger paying off). A non-2xx status, a fetch that failed outright (STATUS 0) and a short inflate are all REFUSED rather than decoded to a partial answer: an empty edition and a failed fetch must never be the same observation. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from inflate: BODY = the decoded 19-column tab-separated gazetteer text, CONTEXT = the job ($GNP header).

inputPorts.description: The decoded gazetteer text with its job. The job rides in the HttpResponse's CONTEXT: ONE size-prefixed $GNP header record geonames-ingest put in the request's CONTEXT and hostcap/http-request echoed - ID = the id prefix, NAME = the text the job decodes (the archive member of a .zip edition, empty = its first member), SOURCE = the dataset contract (DATASET_ID, DATASET_NAME, DATASET_URL, DATASET_EPOCH, SOURCE_URL, SOURCE_QUERY = the file selection, LICENSE, LICENSE_URL, ATTRIBUTION, SHARE_ALIKE, NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY).

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP): the first-order administrative division file (admin1CodesASCII.txt) as fetched; Content-Length, when the origin stated it, must match the BODY.

inputPorts.description: The first-order administrative division file (admin1CodesASCII.txt), as fetched. Optional: a file the flow did not fetch contributes nothing and the affected places carry their codes with the name UNSET.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP): the second-order administrative division file (admin2Codes.txt) as fetched; Content-Length, when the origin stated it, must match the BODY.

inputPorts.description: The second-order administrative division file (admin2Codes.txt), as fetched. Optional: a file the flow did not fetch contributes nothing and the affected places carry their codes with the name UNSET.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP): the country information file (countryInfo.txt) as fetched; Content-Length, when the origin stated it, must match the BODY.

inputPorts.description: The country information file (countryInfo.txt), as fetched. Optional: a file the flow did not fetch contributes nothing and the affected places carry their codes with the name UNSET.

acceptedTypeSets.description: FlowNotice (FNTC): KIND Info, REASON "places-decoded" (or "places-cropped" when the cap cropped the answer), COUNT = records out, SOURCE_NAME = the dataset, AT_MS = its epoch, ITEMS lane=, rows_in=, records_out=, skipped_short_row=, skipped_no_identity=, skipped_out_of_range=, truncated=, dataset_id=, dataset_epoch=, retrieved_at=, admin1_resolved=, admin2_resolved=, countries_resolved=.

outputPorts.description: Run summary: rows in, records out, each skip reason counted, and whether the cap cropped the answer.

methods.description: Decodes the 19-column geoname row shape into $GNP, joining the RESOLVED division and country names from the lookup files on the CC.A1 / CC.A1.A2 / CC keys ($GNP carries a resolved NAME beside every administrative and country code, 'so a consumer need not hold the division tables to render a place'; a lookup miss leaves the name UNSET - a missing name is recoverable, a wrong one is not; a lookup body shorter than its declared Content-Length is refused as lookup-truncated before a row is folded in). The SEED and the DAILY DELTA use this one decoder because modifications-YYYY-MM-DD.txt is a file of FULL geoname rows (verified live 2026-08-15). A job that cannot state DATASET_ID, DATASET_EPOCH and LICENSE is REFUSED (incomplete-dataset-contract), never defaulted: a place published under a guessed epoch is comparable to the wrong bytes. A position outside the WGS 84 domain is DROPPED and counted, never clamped. Columns the gazetteer leaves empty are left UNSET rather than zeroed. RETRIEVED_AT is stamped at decode. Node config geonames_limit (plugin.getConfig; 0 / absent = no cap) crops the record count and the run summary says so. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.displayName: Decode the daily deletes file into tombstones

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from inflate: BODY = the deletes text (geonameid TAB name TAB reason), CONTEXT = the job ($GNP header; its ID is the id prefix).

inputPorts.description: The decoded deletes text with its job.

acceptedTypeSets.description: FlowNotice (FNTC): KIND Info, REASON "tombstones", COUNT = tombstones, SOURCE_NAME = the dataset, AT_MS = its epoch, ITEMS one per tombstone "<record ID>\t<name>\t<reason>" (record ID = <prefix>:<geonameid>, the ID the stored place carries; reason verbatim). When rows were refused, a second FlowNotice REASON "deletes-rows-skipped" COUNT = those rows, ITEMS rows_in=.

outputPorts.description: The tombstone list with each id's verbatim removal reason, plus the refused-row count.

methods.description: Decodes deletes-YYYY-MM-DD.txt (three tab-separated columns, verified live 2026-08-15) into a tombstone list, carrying each removal REASON verbatim because 'duplicate' and 'not a real place' are different facts about the same id. A row whose first column is not a decimal id is skipped and counted - the gazetteer serves an HTML 404 body for a day it no longer retains, and decoding that into tombstones is the exact failure this guard exists for. THIS EMITS A LIST, NOT A DELETION: no host capability removes a stored row (storage-ingest offers ingest only; flatsql-query is read-only) and inventing one would be a new host capability this lane may not add, so the list leaves the flow on its own port as a FlowNotice (no SDS record models a gazetteer tombstone) and the durable delete lane is recorded as a gap rather than faked. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.
